open_questions: Whether an off-target blended binary explains the 17889 ppm QLP events, but depth change alone is sufficient to reject as a target planet
dossier.public_summary: The dip changes from ~1000 ppm to ~18000 ppm between TESS sectors, with the whole signal coming from two huge events in one sector. The duration is also too long for the small M-dwarf host. This is a calibration/blend false alarm, not a repeating planet on the target star.

reasons.why: Depth changes radically between sectors (1031 ppm in sector 35, 1757 ppm in sector 62, 17889 ppm in sector 89).
No real change within a pipeline, but a ~10x deeper dip in the single QLP sector versus both TESS-SPOC sectors. Calibration/or aperture difference, not a planet on target.
reasons.value: differs_by_source TESS-SPOC depth_ppm 1411 err 400 p_constant 0.364 QLP depth_ppm 17889 err 948

reasons.why: Two of six transits out of six are driven by a pair of huge events in QLP sector 89; remaining transits are much shallower, so signal is not repeatable.
reasons.value: p_consistent 5.133252649693772e-56 share_of_top_3 0.986 outliers depth_ppm 19315 sigma 10.8 and 16835 sigma 10.6

reasons.why: Transit longer than a central transit on the 0.46 Rsun M dwarf, and stellar-density mismatch penalty high (star_density_penalty 32.75).

No on-target difference image to confirm location, and with neighbours could_cause 12 (closest 32.1 arcsec delta_mag 4.79), a blended eclipsing binary cannot be ruled out but depth variability favours it.
